evidence: The original presentFor handled only execute and sendKeys and returned `type: detach #${msg.id}` for every other ClientToServer kind, so startFirehose/stopFirehose were mislabeled; 934d260 derives `${msg.kind} #${msg.id}` for all kinds, which is the reviewer's second option and correct by construction.
guidance_note: When a fallthrough return hard-codes one variant's label, enumerate the union's members against it before shipping; derive the label from the discriminant instead of a literal.

evidence: The outbound tests covered only execute and sendKeys, which is why the F1 mislabel shipped; 934d260 added a presentFor case over detach/startFirehose/stopFirehose and a renderPayload case.
guidance_note: When extracting a function over a discriminated union, write one test case per union member, not per branch you remember.

evidence: The quote-wrapped `"${prettyBytes(...)}"` preview is a real but cosmetic ambiguity carried over verbatim from the inlined summarizer and duplicated in DebugPanel; deferring to the SD5 consolidation rather than diverging one of three copies in a behavior-preserving split is a defensible scope call.

The summarizer ended in `return ""` with no exhaustiveness check; the agent deferred to SD5, then in F8 reversed itself saying the fix 'is local to this one function and cheap, and does not conflict with SD5', conceding the single-enforcer/carrying-cost argument did not hold and costing a repeat finding.
guidance_note: Before deferring a finding to a follow-up ticket, check whether the fix is local to code this PR created; an assertNever on a newly extracted function is in scope and a deferral just buys the same finding next round.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: event-summary.test.ts came from the original PR and 934d260 only touched inspector-presentation; the test file covered ~10 of 28 variants and 3f88556 added a table of the rest. behavior-not-structure concerns what tests assert, not how many variants they cover.
guidance_note: When a PR introduces a new test file for an extracted pure function, cover every arm of it in that first commit.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: formatMs (`if (ms < 1) return "<1ms"`) moved out of InspectorView in the original PR and 934d260 did not touch it. The negative-input collapse is real but only reachable via out-of-order timestamps, so 'bug' is overstated; the cheap sign-preserving fix is reasonable, though it left the sub-ms bucket unsigned (F17).
guidance_note: When making a function 'honest across the whole numeric domain', test every bucket with a negative input and make the comment match each branch.

evidence: The `+${formatMs(delta)}` cell was moved from the pre-PR TimelineRow, not changed by 934d260; a negative delta would render `+<1ms`, a real if rare misreport, and 3f88556's formatDelta fixes it.
Flag is a false positive: 3f88556 did not touch event-summary.ts; this is F4 raised again because the agent deferred it, and c91eed2 added an explicit sessions-changed branch plus assertNever.
guidance_note: Accept a cheap exhaustiveness fix on a function the PR just created the first time it is raised, as F4 should have been.

evidence: escapeForDisplay and prettyBytes carried byte-identical escape tables (visible in the c91eed2 removals); c91eed2 extracted escapeByte and routed both through it. The duplication predates the 3f88556 fix it was flagged on.
guidance_note: When a decomposition PR moves two functions next to each other, diff their bodies for duplicated policy before opening the PR.

evidence: The F5 fix (3f88556) added a table commented 'One representative per remaining branch' but omitted unlinked-window-renamed, so the comment's claim was false; fdd0203 added the case. The cited law is about asserting behavior, not coverage counts.
guidance_note: When a fix claims full coverage of a union, generate the case list from the union's members and check it against them instead of writing it from memory.

evidence: The `bytes.length > max` vs `out.length < max` mismatch predates c91eed2 (which only swapped the escape body), so the flag is a false positive on cause; but the agent claimed 'no [LAW:no-silent-failure] issue' and then in F14 conceded 'a truncation with no suffix is a dropped signal' and fixed it in a few lines, so the deferral just bought a repeat finding.
guidance_note: When a reviewer finds a silent-truncation bug in a function the PR already edited, and the fix is a few lines, fix it instead of calling it out of scope.

evidence: Flag is a false positive on cause: the pre-review escapeForDisplay already did `for (const ch of s) { const c = ch.charCodeAt(0); ...}` (visible in c91eed2's removed lines), so the dropped low surrogate predates the F9 fix, which preserved the loop shape. fdd0203 iterates code units and tests an emoji.
guidance_note: When rewriting a loop body to call a per-code-unit helper, check that the loop iterates code units too; for...of over a string yields code points.

evidence: Callers pass Date.now() differences, which are finite, and the pre-F6 formatMs rendered NaN the same way; the reviewer's `return "—"` would hide an upstream bug that a visible 'NaNs' exposes, so the pushback is right.

Flag is a false positive: fdd0203 did not touch format-bytes.ts; this is F11 raised again after the deferral. The repro `prettyBytes(new Uint8Array(30), 48)` renders 12 bytes with no suffix, and 4116318 counts rendered bytes to decide the suffix.
guidance_note: Fix the truncation bug at F11 instead of deferring it.

evidence: `if (c === undefined) break;` on a bounded Uint8Array index predates review (noted as pre-existing in the round 3 summary); the agent confirmed noUncheckedIndexedAccess is off and replaced the loop with `for (const c of bytes)`.

The format-bytes.test.ts added in c91eed2 tested truncation only with printable bytes; this is the test half of the pre-existing F11/F14 bug, not a defect the fix introduced. The cited law concerns what tests assert, not a missing case.
guidance_note: When writing a truncation test, include an input whose rendered length differs from its source length.

evidence: The F6 fix (3f88556) wrote 'the sign is preserved' in formatMs's comment while its sub-ms branch returned bare "<1ms" and its own test pinned `formatMs(-0.4)` to "<1ms"; 4116318 returns `${sign}<1ms`.
guidance_note: When a fix's comment states an invariant like 'sign is preserved', check every branch of the function against it before pushing.

evidence: The reviewer concedes 'the parent-render cascade happens to cover this today', so there is no current defect, and TimelineRow reads only props. The agent's claim that the store back-fills latency by immutable replacement is not visible in the packet. TimelineRow predates fdd0203, so the flag is a false positive.

narrative: A decomposition of InspectorView ran five rounds. Two fixes left gaps the next round caught: the F5 coverage table missed one variant (F10), and the F6 sign-preserving formatMs left its sub-ms bucket unsigned while its comment claimed otherwise (F17). Two deferrals were reversed a round later at trivial cost: F4's assertNever (re-raised as F8) and F11's truncation suffix (re-raised as F14). Every round also brought independent findings on code that only moved, so no round was wholly avoidable.
guidance_observations: Calling a finding out of scope for a 'behavior-preserving decomposition' was used twice on cheap fixes to code the PR itself created or edited, and both were reversed a round later.

Many flagged findings were on code that only moved in the extraction; a pre-PR sweep of the moved functions (exhaustiveness, duplicated escape tables, truncation units) would have caught most rounds 1-4 findings up front.
Fix commits added claims in comments ('one representative per remaining branch', 'sign is preserved') that their own code or tests contradicted.

evidence: No test drove seed() with non-empty trailing while the gate was still buffering, which is the new path SD2 created; 38cf305 adds one asserting SNAP, t1, t2, live in order after the first-resize rAF.
guidance_note: When a change adds a parameter that flows through a gated path, test it in each gate state (buffering and open).

evidence: The diff hunk shows trailing routed through the same write()->bufferWrite path the old PaneStream write loop used, so the stale-pendingWrites edge predates SD2. The agent's reason the proposed reset is unsound (a cached-lastSeed re-attach would drop pending live bytes) is plausible but not verifiable from the packet; it deferred with ticket lkg.21.

Flag is a false positive: 38cf305 only added an xterm-sink test; BufferingSink.seed came from the original PR. The reviewer's 'indistinguishable from live writes' is the intended semantics: XtermSink also unspools trailing through write(), so recording trailing in writes in order mirrors real sink behavior, and a second copy in SeedCall would duplicate it.

The clear-before-seed in the original PR did lose buffered bytes on a sink throw where the old drain loop kept them; the stuck-in-seeding part is pre-existing, so the finding overstates. 6cc6195 clears after the handoff. 38cf305 never touched pane-stream.ts, so the flag is a false positive. A try/catch is not a null guard, so the cited law is stretched.
guidance_note: When a refactor reorders state mutation around an external call, compare its throw-path behavior with the old code before pushing.

evidence: No test combined a non-null cursor (two applySeed writes) with non-empty trailing; 6cc6195 adds it asserting captured -> CUP -> t1 -> t2. The gap is in the original PR's coverage, not created by 38cf305's test.
guidance_note: When a new argument composes with an existing optional one, test the combination, not each alone.

evidence: The `clear(): void` line was unchanged context in the original PR's edit of the TerminalSink block, so this drift predates review; 6cc6195 replaces it with isVisible/dispose to match sink/index.ts.
guidance_note: When editing one line of a doc's interface listing, check the whole listing against the source interface in the same edit.

evidence: Same defect as F4: `this.buffer = []` ran before `liveSink.seed(...)`, losing trailing on a throw. The reviewer's 'swap the reset' option is what 6cc6195 does. Flag is a false positive because 38cf305 did not touch pane-stream.ts.

6cc6195 edited only the TerminalSink block. The missing 'error' event in the PaneStream listing was already noted as pre-existing in the round 0 summary, so the fix did not cause it. The doc has several other unrelated drifts, and declining to sync it to post-design APIs in SD2 is a sound scope call.

narrative: SD2 moved trailing bytes into the seed() call. Round 1 raised the clear-before-seed data-loss ordering from the original PR (F4/F7, one defect), two coverage gaps, a pre-existing doc drift, and a SeedCall shape suggestion the agent rightly rejected. Round 2's one finding asked for more doc syncing in a section the fix had not touched. No finding was caused by a fix commit; all ON-NAMED-FIX flags land on code from the original PR.
guidance_observations: The agent's pushbacks (F2, F3, F8) each named a concrete reason the reviewer's cure was wrong or out of scope, and none were re-raised.
The original PR introduced the clear-before-seed reorder with a comment justifying it on aliasing grounds without checking the throw path the old loop protected.

evidence: The packet does not show markSeedStale's callers, so the claim that `lastSeed === null` always holds here cannot be checked. Dropping the conjunct is still right either way: if it always holds, behavior is unchanged; if not, the branch now re-issues the seed instead of silently keeping a stale screen.

narrative: SD3 collapsed pendingSeed and seedStaleMidFlight into a SeedCycle union. The one finding flagged a redundant inner guard in the stale re-issue branch. The agent removed it and documented the invariant, and round 1 came back clean.
